ai.description: This lizard reaches 45–55 mm SVL. It is brown with a distinct white vertebral stripe and dark lateral blotches. Males possess a large, fan-like, tri-colored dewlap extending to the mid-abdomen.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sitana marudhamneydhal* is best distinguished by its unique dewlap, which features a distinct, vibrant blue patch at the base contrasting with a bright red distal tip.
ai.habitat: *Sitana marudhamneydhal* inhabits the coastal plains and low-lying scrublands of southern India, typically found in sandy, open areas with sparse, dry vegetation.
ai.behavior: *Sitana marudhamneydhal* is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects on the ground during the day while utilizing its cryptic coloration to blend into sand.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sitana marudhamneydhal* is oviparous, laying clutches of 4–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, typically from April to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sitana marudhamneydhal* is endemic to the coastal plains of Tamil Nadu, India, occurring in low-elevation, arid, and semi-arid scrubland habitats.
